The log population ratio has an exact sign-monotone derivative and forbids nonsymmetric periodic orbits. The symmetric equilibrium scalar equation is strictly convex with exact unique minimum; lower-branch determinant is negative. Exchange symmetry gives anti-eigenvalue -xf_x and planar determinant d(2xf_S)-Dxf_x, trace -D-2xf_S+xf_x. For \(d<=2D\), a hypothetical nonnegative upper-branch trace contradicts determinant positivity because 0<xf_x<d. For every \(d>2D\), explicit parameters with a positive equilibrium yield trace zero, positive determinant, nonzero trace parameter derivative. At the exact tuple (1,5,11,3/5,19,160) the linear eigenvalues are -19/4,±i sqrt(14), and exact cubic normal-form differentiation independently verifies canonical first Lyapunov coefficient -40879/532480, so a stable positive limit cycle is born for \(K<3/5\) along m=100(1+K). For \(d<=D\) strict Bendixson-Dulac divergence in the positive symmetric plane and the ratio identity exclude periodic orbits, with omega-limit alternatives yielding convergence to equilibrium. SymPy verify.py was executed successfully from the actual new package. The analytic argument, not finite computation, supplies the universal conclusions. Ambiguous dynamic nondegeneracy at the equilibrium fold is not asserted beyond the strict scalar quadratic tangency.

originality.rationale: The complete arXiv:2603.11002v1 motivating paper establishes the model, generic equilibrium theory/Routh-Hurwitz formulas and numerical Hopf bifurcations with unequal parameters; source Section 4 assumes D1=D2=D. This finding is the exact exchange-symmetric positive Monod equal-biomass-removal subfamily with D1=D2=d not necessarily D. Its new combined claim is a sharp universal local Hopf feasibility criterion \(d>2D\), explicit constructive family, rigorously negative cubic Hopf witness with stable synchronized cycles, and a global non-oscillation/convergence subregime \(d<=D\). The 2009 El Hajji et al. full text establishes global dynamics and Dulac arguments only for the endpoint \(d=D\); none of its conclusions directly implies a \(d>2D\) example or rules out an unequal-retention oscillation barrier. Generic local Routh-Hurwitz criteria, fold multiplicity concepts, and \(d=D\) no-cycle facts are acknowledged antecedents, not claimed new. Published same-domain research summaries concerned a serial two-reactor AM2 system or mutation-weighted growth, not the same obligate mutualists.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper attributes oscillatory coexistence to mortality/retention differences in an obligate mutualism reactor. A mathematically and biologically natural simplification asks whether a biomass rate common to both species, but distinct from nutrient dilution, permits cycles. The theorem proves a sharp necessary-and-feasible local Hopf boundary \(d>2D\) for the entire symmetric Monod family, gives an explicit valid supercritical cycle, and separates a global \(d<=D\) non-oscillation regime. The sharp distinction between species-rate asymmetry and common excess removal is structurally relevant to mechanistic reactor modeling, not a known-table result, arbitrary parameter slice, or textbook corollary. No empirical application or guaranteed cycles for all \(d>2D\) is claimed.
